---
title: Layout and chrome
description: Compose AppLayout, the title bar, the status bar, and the search bar around your content.
---

```tsx title="service-status.tsx"
import { useMode } from "@tooee/commands";
import { AppLayout } from "@tooee/layout";
import { launchCli, useQuitCommand, useThemeCommands } from "@tooee/shell";
import { useTheme } from "@tooee/themes";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

interface Service {
  name: string;
  healthy: boolean;
}

const services: Service[] = [
  { healthy: true, name: "api" },
  { healthy: true, name: "web" },
  { healthy: false, name: "worker" },
];

const ServiceStatus = function ServiceStatus(): ReactNode {
  const { theme } = useTheme();
  const mode = useMode();
  const { name: themeName } = useThemeCommands();
  useQuitCommand();

  return (
    <AppLayout
      titleBar={{ subtitle: "eu-west", title: "Service status" }}
      statusBar={{
        items: [
          { label: "Theme:", value: themeName },
          { label: "Mode:", value: mode },
          { label: "", value: "t theme  q quit" },
        ],
      }}
    >
      <box flexDirection="column" paddingLeft={1}>
        {services.map(
          (service): ReactNode => (
            <text
              key={service.name}
              content={`${service.name.padEnd(8)} ${service.healthy ? "ok" : "degraded"}`}
              fg={service.healthy ? theme.success : theme.warning}
            />
          ),
        )}
      </box>
    </AppLayout>
  );
};

await launchCli(<ServiceStatus />);
```

Run it with `bun service-status.tsx`. The title bar reads `Service status — eu-west`, the three services fill the middle, and the status bar shows the theme and the mode. Press `t`: the theme picker opens over the content, and the `Theme:` item follows your choice. `q` quits.

`AppLayout` from `@tooee/layout` is a column the size of the terminal: the title bar, a content area that takes the remaining height, and the status bar or the search bar at the bottom. The current overlay and the toasts draw over the content area. `useThemeCommands` and `useQuitCommand` come from `@tooee/shell`; [Your first Tooee app](/docs/build/first-app#add-the-chrome) introduces them. `<box>` and `<text>` are [OpenTUI](https://opentui.com) elements.

## Title bar

`titleBar` takes `{ title, subtitle }`. The title draws in `theme.primary`, then a dash and the subtitle in `theme.textMuted`, all on `theme.backgroundPanel`. Omit the prop and the content area starts on the first line. `TitleBar` is exported for a layout of your own and takes the same two props.

The title bar stays on one row. When the terminal is narrow, the subtitle shortens with an ellipsis first. Below 8 cells the subtitle hides, and then the title shortens. `fitTitleBar(title, subtitle, width)` returns the text that the bar draws at that width.

## Status bar

`statusBar` is required and takes `{ items }`. Each item is `{ label, value }`: the label draws muted, the value follows it in the text colour, and two columns separate one item from the next. An empty `label` with a `value` draws plain text, which is how the example shows its key hints. `StatusBar` is exported. It takes `items`, `hiddenMarker`, and an optional `width` in cells, which defaults to the terminal width.

The status bar stays on one row. These optional item fields control what happens when the items do not fit:

| Field           | Meaning                                                                                                         |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `priority`      | A number. Items with a higher value stay longer. The default is `0`. `StatusPriority` names a shared scale.    |
| `align`         | `"end"` puts the item in a group at the right edge. The default is `"start"`.                                  |
| `compact`       | `{ label?, value? }`, a shorter form that the bar uses before it shortens or hides an item.                    |
| `truncate`      | `"end"`, `"start"`, or `"middle"`: where the ellipsis goes when the value shortens. Without it the value keeps its full length. |
| `minValueWidth` | The smallest value width in cells after truncation. The default is `8`.                                        |
| `id`            | A stable React key.                                                                                             |

When the items are too wide, the bar first switches items to their `compact` form, lowest priority first. Then, lowest priority first, it shortens a value that has `truncate` down to `minValueWidth`, and hides the item if the bar still overflows. On equal priority the item further right goes first. One item always stays, and its value shortens to fit. Last, visible items get their full form back where there is room. A `⋯` after the start group shows that items are hidden. Pass `hiddenMarker` to `statusBar` or to `StatusBar` to use another glyph, or `false` to show none.

`StatusPriority` holds the values `critical` (4), `position` (3), `focus` (2), `content` (1), `background` (0), and `hint` (-1). Give key hints `hint`, so they go first. Use `truncate: "start"` for file paths, `"middle"` for ids such as model names, and `"end"` for free text. `fitStatusBar(items, width)` returns the layout that the bar draws, so a test can check it without a renderer. `truncateCells(text, width, mode)` is the helper both bars use to shorten text by terminal cells.

`DocumentScreen` fills this bar itself. It draws the theme and its `statusItems` at the start, and the mode and the cursor at the right edge. [Documents](/docs/build/documents#draw-the-rows) lists the order. In Tooee 0.12 and earlier, the bar wraps onto a second row when the items do not fit, and the item fields above do not exist.

## Scroll the content

Without `scroll`, the content area is a box that clips what does not fit. Pass `scroll` to put the content in a scrollbox:

| Field          | Default | Meaning                                                                         |
| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ref`          |         | Required. A `RefObject<ScrollBoxRenderable>` for reading or setting the scroll. |
| `stickyScroll` | `false` | Follow new content at the end until you scroll away from it.                    |
| `stickyStart`  |         | `"bottom"` or `"top"`: the end the sticky view starts at.                       |
| `focused`      | `true`  | Give the scrollbox keyboard focus, so the arrow keys and page keys scroll it.   |

```tsx title="build-log.tsx"
import type { ScrollBoxRenderable } from "@opentui/core";
import { AppLayout } from "@tooee/layout";
import { launchCli, useQuitCommand } from "@tooee/shell";
import { useEffect, useRef, useState } from "react";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const BuildLog = function BuildLog(): ReactNode {
  const scrollRef = useRef<ScrollBoxRenderable | null>(null);
  const [lines, setLines] = useState<string[]>([]);
  useQuitCommand();

  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = setInterval(() => {
      setLines((previous) => [...previous, `[${previous.length + 1}] compiled module`]);
    }, 200);
    return () => {
      clearInterval(timer);
    };
  }, []);

  return (
    <AppLayout
      titleBar={{ title: "Build log" }}
      statusBar={{ items: [{ label: "Lines:", value: String(lines.length) }] }}
      scroll={{ ref: scrollRef, stickyScroll: true, stickyStart: "bottom" }}
    >
      {lines.map(
        (line): ReactNode => (
          <text key={line} content={line} />
        ),
      )}
    </AppLayout>
  );
};

await launchCli(<BuildLog />);
```

The log grows five lines a second and the view stays on the newest line. The wheel scrolls it, and the `Lines:` count keeps rising in the status bar.

`AppLayout` takes its scrollbox ref and options through the `scroll` prop. Leave `scroll` unset when the content is a `Document` or a `MarkdownView`: the row document is a scrollbox of its own and follows the cursor.

## Side region

`aside` takes a node that `AppLayout` draws to the right of the content. The title bar and the status bar stay full width, and the overlay covers the content and the aside together. Give the aside a `width`; the content takes the rest.

```tsx title="release-notes.tsx"
import { AppLayout } from "@tooee/layout";
import { launchCli, useQuitCommand } from "@tooee/shell";
import { useTheme } from "@tooee/themes";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const sections = ["Fixes", "Features", "Upgrade notes"];

const ReleaseNotes = function ReleaseNotes(): ReactNode {
  const { theme } = useTheme();
  useQuitCommand();

  return (
    <AppLayout
      titleBar={{ title: "Release notes" }}
      statusBar={{ items: [{ label: "", value: "q quit" }] }}
      aside={
        <box width={24} flexDirection="column" border={["left"]} borderColor={theme.border}>
          {sections.map(
            (section): ReactNode => (
              <text key={section} content={section} fg={theme.textMuted} paddingLeft={1} />
            ),
          )}
        </box>
      }
    >
      <text content="Tooee 0.12 adds folds and a heading outline to View." paddingLeft={1} />
    </AppLayout>
  );
};

await launchCli(<ReleaseNotes />);
```

`DocumentScreen` takes the same `aside` prop and passes it on. View draws its heading outline in this region.

## Search bar

`searchBar` takes a `SearchState`, the object `controller.search` holds on a [document](/docs/build/documents#search) or `useSearch` returns. While `searchActive` is `true`, `AppLayout` draws `SearchBar` from `@tooee/search` in place of the status bar: a `/` prompt, a focused input bound to `setSearchQuery`, `Enter` bound to `submitSearch`, and a count such as `2/5` or `No matches`. `DocumentScreen` passes `controller.search` for you.

A layout of your own mounts `SearchBar` with these props:

| Prop            | Meaning                                                                                                     |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `query`         | The text in the input.                                                                                      |
| `onQueryChange` | Called with the new text on every keystroke.                                                                |
| `onSubmit`      | Called on `Enter`.                                                                                          |
| `onCancel`      | Optional and deprecated. The bar never calls it; `Escape` cancels through the `search-cancel` command. A later release removes it. In 0.12 and earlier the prop is required. |
| `matchCount`    | Number of matches. `0` with a non-empty query draws `No matches`.                                           |
| `currentMatch`  | Index of the current match, drawn one-based.                                                                |

## Overlays and toasts

`AppLayout` calls `useCurrentOverlay()` from `@tooee/overlays` and draws the result in a box the size of the content area, above the content. The command palette, the which-key bar, the theme picker, the context menu, the Ask and Choose dialogs, and any overlay you open with `useOverlay().open` land there. `ToastContainer` from `@tooee/toasts` sits in the bottom right corner of the same area and draws the toast that `ctx.toast?.toast(...)` sends.

`AppLayout` has no `overlay` prop in 0.13. The `@tooee/layout` README still describes one as deprecated; code that passed an element to it opens the overlay through the store instead. [Overlays, dialogs, and toasts](/docs/build/overlays-dialogs-toasts) covers `open`, roles, and dialogs.

A layout of your own has to mount both. This one keeps the title bar and the status bar from `@tooee/layout`, adds the search bar, and draws the overlay and the toasts over a document:

```tsx title="custom-chrome.tsx"
import { useMode } from "@tooee/commands";
import { StatusBar, TitleBar } from "@tooee/layout";
import { useCurrentOverlay } from "@tooee/overlays";
import { SearchBar } from "@tooee/search";
import {
  Document,
  launchCli,
  useDocumentController,
  useQuitCommand,
  useThemeCommands,
} from "@tooee/shell";
import { useTheme } from "@tooee/themes";
import { ToastContainer } from "@tooee/toasts";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const hosts = ["alpha.internal", "beta.internal", "gamma.internal", "delta.internal"];

const HostList = function HostList(): ReactNode {
  const { theme } = useTheme();
  const mode = useMode();
  const overlay = useCurrentOverlay();
  useThemeCommands();
  useQuitCommand();
  const controller = useDocumentController({
    adapter: { getText: (host: string) => host },
    rows: hosts,
    search: {},
  });
  const { search } = controller;
  const handleSearchQueryChange = (query: string): void => {
    search?.setSearchQuery(query);
  };
  const handleSearchSubmit = (): void => {
    search?.submitSearch();
  };
  const handleSearchCancel = (): void => {
    search?.setSearchQuery("");
  };

  return (
    <box flexDirection="column" width="100%" height="100%" backgroundColor={theme.background}>
      <TitleBar title="Hosts" />
      <box style={{ flexGrow: 1, position: "relative" }}>
        <Document
          controller={controller}
          style={{ flexGrow: 1 }}
          renderRow={(host): ReactNode => <text content={` ${host}`} />}
        />
        {overlay !== null && (
          <box position="absolute" left={0} top={0} width="100%" height="100%">
            {overlay}
          </box>
        )}
        <ToastContainer />
      </box>
      {search?.searchActive === true ? (
        <SearchBar
          query={search.searchQuery}
          onQueryChange={handleSearchQueryChange}
          onSubmit={handleSearchSubmit}
          onCancel={handleSearchCancel}
          matchCount={search.matchingLines.length}
          currentMatch={search.currentMatchIndex}
        />
      ) : (
        <StatusBar
          items={[
            { label: "Mode:", value: mode },
            { label: "Rows:", value: String(hosts.length) },
          ]}
        />
      )}
    </box>
  );
};

await launchCli(<HostList />);
```

`/` swaps the status bar for the search bar, `t` opens the theme picker inside the relative box, and `y y` shows its toast in the corner. Overlays position themselves with percentages, so the box that holds them needs `position: "relative"` and the full content size.

## Overlay panels and the close button

`OverlayPanel` from `@tooee/layout` is the bordered panel the Ask and Choose dialogs and panels draw. Use it for an overlay of your own:

```tsx title="shortcuts-panel.tsx"
import { useCommand } from "@tooee/commands";
import { AppLayout, OverlayPanel } from "@tooee/layout";
import { useOverlay } from "@tooee/overlays";
import { launchCli, useQuitCommand } from "@tooee/shell";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";

const Shortcuts = function Shortcuts(): ReactNode {
  const overlay = useOverlay();
  useQuitCommand();
  useCommand({
    handler: () => {
      overlay.open(
        "shortcuts",
        ({ close }): ReactNode => (
          <OverlayPanel
            title="Shortcuts"
            hints="Escape closes"
            inset={{ bottom: "30%", left: "25%", right: "25%", top: "30%" }}
            onClose={() => {
              close();
            }}
          >
            <box flexDirection="column" paddingLeft={1}>
              <text content="?   show this panel" />
              <text content="q   quit" />
            </box>
          </OverlayPanel>
        ),
        null,
      );
    },
    hotkey: "?",
    id: "help.shortcuts",
    title: "Shortcuts",
  });

  return (
    <AppLayout
      titleBar={{ title: "Shortcuts demo" }}
      statusBar={{ items: [{ label: "", value: "? help  q quit" }] }}
    >
      <box paddingLeft={1}>
        <text content="Press ? for the shortcut list." />
      </box>
    </AppLayout>
  );
};

await launchCli(<Shortcuts />);
```

`?` opens the panel over the content. `Escape` closes it, and so does a click on the `✕` in its title row. The panel props:

| Prop          | Meaning                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `title`       | Title row content. A string draws in `theme.accent`; a node draws as given.                                  |
| `prompt`      | Bold text, or a node, between the title row and the body.                                                    |
| `children`    | The body.                                                                                                    |
| `footer`      | One row below the body.                                                                                      |
| `hints`       | Left side of the bottom row, muted.                                                                          |
| `statusRight` | Right side of the bottom row, muted.                                                                         |
| `inset`       | `{ left, right, top, bottom }` as a number, a percentage string, or `"auto"`. Each side defaults to `"20%"`. |
| `onClose`     | Shows a `CloseButton` in the title row and runs when it is clicked.                                          |
| `onMouseDown` | Mouse handler for the whole panel.                                                                           |

`CloseButton` takes `onClose`, an optional `glyph` in place of `✕`, and an optional `color`. It reacts to the left button only and stops the click from reaching the panel behind it. Tooee 0.8 moved it from `@tooee/themes` to `@tooee/layout`; the palette, the theme picker, and the Choose filter draw the same button. [Panels](/docs/build/panels) covers panel groups, which have chrome of their own.
